title: Exceptional coefficient construction: finite scalar mates
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R_E$, uniformizers $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed separated over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,A}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the actual full category of bounded constructible constant-$A$ complexes with finite Tor amplitude, and $I_{T,A}$ for its full inclusion [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_A=Rp_{c,*}j_!$ and $G_A=\nu_X^*f^\times_{c,A}R\nu_{Y,*}$, using the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Equip these functors with the transported adjunction and adjoint shift structures. For every unital finite coefficient map $a:A\to B$ between the rings $A_{E,n}$ (including quotients and ramified maps $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,en}$), the ambient derived extension $S_{a,T}=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ preserves $\mathcal C_{T,A}$ and its Tor interval. It admits the literal full-subcategory restriction $T_{a,T}$, so $I_{T,B}T_{a,T}=S_{a,T}I_{T,A}$ is an equality of functors and its realization is the equality isomorphism. There are invertible shift-compatible comparisons
$$q_a:T_{a,Y}F_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_{a,X},\qquad b_a:T_{a,X}G_A\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_{a,Y}.$$
The first is exactly the proper scalar-adjunction mate followed by the open tensor map, transported from etale to pro-etale by the canonical proper/open comparisons. The second is the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_{a,Y}\epsilon_A\circ q_{a,G_A}^{-1}$, so
$$\epsilon_{B,T_{a,Y}L}\circ F_B(b_{a,L})\circ q_{a,G_AL}=T_{a,Y}(\epsilon_{A,L}).$$
This assertion includes nonflat quotients. On restriction of scalars the right map is the constant-$B$ exceptional tensor comparison, through the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Res}_XG_B\cong G_A\operatorname{Res}_Y$. All realizations use the same counits, site-comparison units and flat-model pullback/tensor identifications; the proper projection and open maps preserve their shifts.

proof.text: First work on the ordinary etale categories. For $K\in\mathcal C_{T,A}$, constructible origin and Tor comparison give an etale object $K^e$ with the same Tor interval $[u,v]$. The constructible variant of the flat-model lemma applies because $T$ is finite type over $k$: choose a flat constructible model $P$ supported in $[u,v]$. A bounded complex of flat sheaves is K-flat, so derived change of rings computes $K^e\otimes_A^LB$ by $P\otimes_AB$, canonically on morphisms and independently of this model. Each term is flat over $B$: for an injection $M\hookrightarrow N$ of $B$-module sheaves, $(P^i\otimes_AB)\otimes_BM=P^i\otimes_A\operatorname{Res}M$, and flatness of $P^i$ preserves this injection. On any stratum trivializing $P^i$, its tensor with the finite ring $B$ is finite locally constant. Take a common finite refinement for the finitely many terms. The constructible Serre theorem gives constructible kernels, images and cohomology. The same flat complex supported in $[u,v]$ therefore has Tor interval $[u,v]$ over $B$, including for nonflat $A\to B$.

source.place: Finite coefficient tensor; Proposition 2.29; flat-model argument made explicit.

proof.text: Exact comparison inverse image and the canonical derived pullback/tensor identification identify $\nu_T^*(P\otimes_AB)$ with $S_{a,T}(\nu_T^*P)$. The constructible-origin and Tor-comparison theorems carry the conclusion of step 1 back to the actual pro-etale category, with the unchanged interval. Define $T_{a,T}$ on objects by the ambient $S_{a,T}$ with this membership proof and on morphisms by $S_{a,T}$ itself. The subcategory is full, so identities and composition are literally those of the ambient functor: $I_{T,B}T_{a,T}=S_{a,T}I_{T,A}$, with equality realization. Exactness and its canonical shifts are inherited from derived change of rings. This construction applies separately to every actual finite ring map, including an identity or a composite.

proof.text: Write $F^e_R=Rp_{c,\mathrm{et},R,*}j^e_{!,R}$ and $G^e_R=f^\times_{c,R}$ on the entire etale derived categories. Use their ambient adjunctions, with counits $\epsilon^e_R$. Let $q^e_a$ be exactly the proper coefficient comparison at $j^e_{!,A}(-)$ followed by $Rp_{c,B,*}$ of the open scalar tensor map. The proper comparison theorem specifies its transpose as scalar extension of the proper counit after the canonical pullback/tensor identification; the open map is scalar balancing on the open and zero off it. The compact scalar coherence theorem proves this specified composite invertible for any finite $A\to B$, with no flatness assumption. Thus $q^e_a:S_YF^e_A\cong F^e_BS_X$ is the required left map rather than an independently chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings; proper scalar map with its specified counit normalization.

proof.text:
Put $U_T=\operatorname{Res}_{a,T}$. Derived ringed direct-image composition applied to the two factorizations of the same ringed-topos map gives $U_YRp_{c,B,*}\cong Rp_{c,A,*}U_{\overline X}$. Open extension by zero commutes with $U$ termwise: it changes only the ring action on the open and both sides are zero off the open. Consequently $h:U_YF^e_B\cong F^e_AU_X$ is the canonical restriction comparison. For any $N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the scalar adjunction, the two exceptional adjunctions and $q^e_a$ give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,U_XG^e_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_XK,G^e_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(F^e_BS_XK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_YF^e_AK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,G^e_AU_YN).$$
Yoneda gives a canonical isomorphism $d_N:U_XG^e_BN\cong G^e_AU_YN$. Explicitly $d_N$ is the transpose of $F^e_AU_XG^e_BN\xrightarrow{h^{-1}}U_YF^e_BG^e_BN\xrightarrow{U_Y\epsilon^e_{B,N}}U_YN$. Indeed, following $\mathrm{id}$ through the chain, its image is $U_Y(\epsilon^e_{B,N}F^e_B(c)\,q^e)\circ\eta$, with $\eta:x\mapsto x\otimes1$ the scalar unit and $c:x\otimes b\mapsto b\,x$ the scalar counit. By the proper coefficient theorem and the open balancing map, $h\circ U_Yq^e_K$ is the projection map $P_K:B_Y\otimes^L_AF^e_AK\to F^e_A(B_X\otimes^L_AK)$. Naturality of $h$ then rewrites the image as $U_Y\epsilon^e_{B,N}\,h^{-1}\,F^e_A(U_Xc)\,P\,\eta$. Since $P$ is natural in the constant factor and is the identity for the unit $A$, $F^e_A(U_Xc)\,P\,\eta=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings, restriction square; Zheng Proposition 2.23; normalized scalar adjunction.

proof.text:
For $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define $b^e_{a,L}$ to be the $F^e_B\dashv G^e_B$ transpose of
$$F^e_BS_XG^e_AL\xrightarrow{(q^e_{a,G^e_AL})^{-1}}S_YF^e_AG^e_AL\xrightarrow{S_Y\epsilon^e_{A,L}}S_YL.$$
The adjunction bijection gives naturality in $L$ and exactly
$$\epsilon^e_{B,S_YL}\,F^e_B(b^e_{a,L})\,q^e_{a,G^e_AL}=S_Y\epsilon^e_{A,L}.$$
Under $d_{S_YL}$ and $U_TS_T(-)=B_T\otimes_A^L(-)$, its restriction has $F^e_A$-transpose
$$F^e_A(B_X\otimes_A^LG^e_AL)\xrightarrow{P^{-1}}B_Y\otimes_A^LF^e_AG^e_AL\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon^e_{A,L}}B_Y\otimes_A^LL.$$
Indeed substitute the transpose formula for $d$ from step 4 into the preceding counit equation; $U_Yq^e$ is $P$, since its proper factor is precisely the ordered projection by the proper coefficient theorem and its open factor is the balancing map. Naturality of $h$ and the counit equation replace $U_Y\epsilon^e_B\,U_YF^e_B(b^e)$ by $U_YS_Y\epsilon^e_A\,(U_Yq^e)^{-1}$. This is the displayed formula. It is the defining transpose of the exceptional constant-$B$ tensor map. The constant-tensor theorem applies to $B\in D(A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ without requiring perfection or bounded projective dimension, so this restricted map is invertible. Restriction detects quasi-isomorphisms: the cohomology of a cone is unchanged as an abelian sheaf. Hence the $B$-linear map $b^e_a$ is invertible.

proof.text:
The finite-operations theorem supplies the actual constructible restrictions of $F_R,G_R$, their adjunction and their adjoint shift structures, without absolute separatedness. Steps 1–2 apply both to its inputs and to $F_RK,G_RL$, so every endpoint of $q,b$ lies in the stated full categories. Use constructible origin and the invertible bounded-below site-comparison unit to transport $q^e,b^e$ through $
u^*$ and $R
u_*$. The compact-support comparison identifies $
u_Y^*F^e_R$ with $F_R
u_X^*$; the exceptional realization is $G_R=
u_X^*G^e_RR
u_{Y,*}$. Its unit and counit are precisely those of the transported adjunction. Applying the equivalence to the equation in step 5 therefore gives
$$\epsilon_{B,T_{a,Y}L}F_B(b_{a,L})q_{a,G_AL}=T_{a,Y}(\epsilon_{A,L}).$$
Fullness identifies the transported arrows with natural transformations on the actual full subcategories, and full faithfulness makes this the unique transpose there.

source.place: Tags 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, and 09B1, lemma-compare-derived; exceptional definition, finite-stage transported adjunction.

proof.text: For the realization of $q$, expand the compact-support site comparison into its two factors. The proper factor is the counit-normalized direct-image mate, not an unspecified site isomorphism. The open factor is the termwise comparison $\nu_{\overline X}^*j^e_!\cong j^p_!\nu_X^*$. Substitute their defining counit and open-unit transposes into step 3. The adjacent site units cancel with the site counits, and the remaining proper transpose is the scalar extension of the same proper counit followed by the same open balancing map. The tensor/pullback comparison identifies the intervening tensors on K-flat models. Thus this transport is exactly the pro-etale proper scalar-adjunction mate followed by the open tensor map. The counit equation of step 6 then identifies $b$ with its required normalized transpose; no second choice of Hom bijections is introduced. The restriction description in step 5 transports to etale-origin objects using these same identifications and site units.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; proper site mate and termwise open comparison, normalized by their counits/units.

proof.text: All shift equations use the chosen derived shifts. Derived change of rings is exact. The pullback/tensor comparison commutes with integer shifts; the proper projection map commutes with shifts in the direct-image input by the first-variable projection theorem (and in the tensor input by the ringed projection theorem). For the proper scalar map, transpose its proposed shift equation: its counit formula and the pullback/tensor shift equation give identical transposes, hence equal maps. This uses the scalar map itself and does not infer equality from restriction of scalars. The open map is induced by the degreewise balancing identity. On the total tensor complexes both paths shift the same summand and have the same tensor sign, so it commutes with shifts in either input. The site comparison is termwise on inverse images and its direct-image comparison is the mate using the adjoint shifts. Composition and whiskering preserve shift equations. Consequently $q$ has the required shift equation. Transpose the two sides of the proposed shift equation for $b$: by shift compatibility of the fixed counits, each transpose is $T_Y\epsilon_A\,(q_{G_A})^{-1}$ with the same shift identifications. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection makes the two arrows equal. This also proves compatibility for every integer, with the unique adjoint shift structure.
